html:
A church of "Holy Peace" in Constantinople, rebuilt by Justinian after the Nika riots of 532 burned the older church on the site. The older church had hosted the First Council of Constantinople in 381.

Justinian's church was a domed basilica near Hagia Sophia. It was badly damaged in the earthquake of 740 and restored by Constantine V. Because he was an opponent of holy images, the apse shows only a large plain cross, a rare surviving piece of Iconoclast art.

After 1453 the Ottomans did not make it a mosque. It stood inside the outer court of Topkapı Palace and served as an armoury. That is why it keeps its church form, one of very few in Istanbul. Today it is a museum and concert hall.
sum: A church of "Holy Peace" in Constantinople, rebuilt by Justinian after the Nika riots of 532 burned the older church on the site. The older church had hosted the First Council of Constantinople in 381.
